D22·ye47 — 2026-09-23
rule: A session the host slept through or that was stopped from outside is never scored; the evaluator records each session's regime and never gates on the prompt hash.
chose: 3.6 applies round 2's rules in the evaluator's own code, and the pin stays where it is. L22 (the host slept) or L24 (the agent was stopped from outside) during an agent session makes it a HARNESS FAILURE: the session's work is discarded, a harness-*.json is written, the run stops with exit 5, and --resume re-runs the session. A score the host slept through is taken once more; if the host sleeps through the second pass too, the result carries score_invalid and compare skips it. The regime (Claude Code version, normalised prompt hash, auto_mode steer flags, foreign instruction files) is RECORDED in every run and fix result and never enforced. L25 seals sibling runs with a require-not rule, which also covers runs created later. L21 uses a per-cell ZDOTDIR that puts the pinned runner's SOFAR_BIN_DIR and the claude shim first.
over: (a) Scoring a slept-through or externally stopped session as an agent failure, which is what round 1 did and what L22/L24 record as a loss. (b) Enforcing the prompt hash or the steer. The hash moves within one version for reasons outside the experimenter's control (note 01M35N82X0), so gating on it turns the gate into noise; round 2 enforces the steer only against a per-arm reference, which the evaluator has no source for yet. (c) Listing the existing sibling runs in the profile, which misses a run started after the profile was written. (d) Importing round 2's shellpin/hostpower/validity from handoff-bench, which would move the pin.
because: Each rule is round 2's measured fix, carried over as the evaluator's own code, so the guard column no longer inherits those round-1 losses while the pin (handoff-bench c628b55, the eight modules) and its comparability stay intact. A stop-and-resume costs one re-launch, while a mis-scored session silently corrupts a verdict.
